bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` at `fuzz/fuzz_die_cu_attrs.c:185` in the staged vulnerable `libdwarf-code` checkout `8bf96199a0e130483cceca6bfacfbe4127441ab1`. The exact staged witness is a 279-byte ELF-like file (sha256 `7e45353413b620d70e937a7ea5f7054577ad149493a7456f8c5d7a714c511326`) that the harness writes to `/tmp/libfuzzer.$pid` and reopens through libdwarf. On the crashing run, `dwarf_next_cu_header_d(..., is_info = 0)` makes libdwarf load `.debug_types`; the saved ASan allocation stack ties the later freed pointer to the 48-byte section buffer allocated in `elf_load_nolibelf_section()` and reached via `_dwarf_load_debug_types()`. Later `dwarf_diename(cu_die, &name, errp)` resolves the DIE name through `dwarf_formstring()` and returns `name` as a direct alias into that loaded section, not as caller-owned heap storage. Vulnerable `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` then unconditionally executes `free(name)` at line 185. ASan reports the freed address as `0x60400000012d`, which is 29 bytes inside the section allocation `[0x604000000110,0x604000000140)`. The staged patch fixes this exact ownership bug by removing the inappropriate `free(name)` calls from the test source.

source.description: First non-harness project read on the vulnerable path: libdwarf copies attacker-controlled section bytes from the temporary file into the heap buffer that later backs the freed interior pointer.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 279-byte file the harness writes and reopens. Its prefix begins with an ELF header and section names such as `.debug_types.dwo`, and the saved ASan allocation stack shows the later freed pointer comes from this section load.
source.note: On the crashing run `_dwarf_next_cu_header_internal(..., is_info = 0)` reaches `_dwarf_load_debug_types()`, which calls this loader. The resulting 48-byte allocation is the region ASan later reports around the bad-free target.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The fuzzer source passes a borrowed libdwarf string pointer to `free()` even though that pointer aliases the loaded `.debug_types` section buffer rather than caller-owned heap.
sink.note: Stage 01's ASan trace reports `free()` on `0x60400000012d`, 29 bytes inside the 48-byte region allocated at `elf_load_nolibelf_section:230` while loading `.debug_types`.

root_cause.description: The caller-side test source treats `dwarf_diename()`'s returned name as malloc-owned and unconditionally frees it. The staged patch removes this call because libdwarf may return section-backed strings that must not be freed by the caller.
root_cause.note: The crashing path uses the later `free(name)` at line 185, not the earlier dead `free(name)` in the `if (res == DW_DLV_ERROR || res == DW_DLV_NO_ENTRY)` block where `res` was just shadow-initialized to `0`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Libdwarf materializes the value later passed to `free()` here by returning a direct pointer into the currently loaded `.debug_types` data instead of allocating a copy.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The saved ASan bad-free address lies inside the 48-byte `.debug_types` allocation from `elf_load_nolibelf_section()`, so the returned `name` must alias bytes inside that section buffer rather than separate heap storage.
tainted_value_origin.note: This is the `DW_FORM_string` case in `dwarf_formstring()`. The comments in `dwarf_form.c` and `dwarf_alloc.c` explicitly describe such returned strings as section-backed and not caller-freed.

parser_admitted.description: The temporary file passes `dwarf_init_b()` and `dwarf_next_cu_header_d()` far enough to enter the CU-processing block that later calls `dwarf_diename()` and reaches the bad free.
parser_admitted.note: The saved allocation stack reaches `_dwarf_next_cu_header_internal()` from `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput:71`, and the crashing run continues through the nested CU/DIE block to line 185.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation and relies only on the staged source, patch, reproduction report, and saved ASan traces.
Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though the staged diff removes the exact `free(name)` call reached by the reproduced crash.

The saved artifacts do not dump the precise DIE abbreviation bytes, so the `DW_FORM_string` arm is grounded from the source plus allocator evidence: the bad-free target lies inside the `.debug_types` allocation returned by `elf_load_nolibelf_section()`, which matches `dwarf_formstring()` returning `begin` directly from the current section.

coarse_trace.summary: While processing the attacker file as `is_info = 0`, libdwarf loads `.debug_types` bytes into a 48-byte heap buffer.
The DIE name is resolved through the `DW_FORM_string` path, which returns a direct alias into that loaded section instead of allocating a new string.
The fuzzer stores that borrowed pointer in local `name` via `dwarf_diename()` and continues to later cleanup without converting it to owned storage.
The test source unconditionally executes `free(name)`, and ASan reports a bad-free on the interior `.debug_types` pointer.

fine_trace.note: Source. Libdwarf reads attacker-controlled bytes from the temporary file into `sp->gh_content`, the heap buffer backing the `.debug_types` section for this run. ASan later identifies the bad-free target as an interior pointer into this exact allocation.

In the `DW_FORM_string` case, `dwarf_formstring()` returns `begin` directly from the currently loaded section instead of allocating a copy. On the reproduced run the later freed address is 29 bytes inside step 1's 48-byte allocation, so the returned string aliases that section buffer.
The borrowed section pointer from step 2 is written into local `name`. No ownership conversion happens here; `name` simply aliases the libdwarf-managed section bytes returned by `dwarf_diename()`.

Root cause and sink. The caller passes the borrowed pointer from step 3 to `free()`. ASan reports that pointer as `0x60400000012d`, 29 bytes inside the section allocation created at step 1, so this is a bad-free of interior, non-owned memory.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged diff removes both `free(name)` calls from `fuzz/fuzz_die_cu_attrs.c`, including the observed sink at line 185. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, so this remains source-grounded rather than dynamically confirmed.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan trace's first project frame is `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` at `fuzz_die_cu_attrs.c:185`, the same `free(name)` call recorded as the sink.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The allocator stack shows `name` points into the section allocation created by `elf_load_nolibelf_section`; the bug is the caller-side ownership mistake of freeing that borrowed pointer at line 185.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved allocation stack `elf_load_nolibelf_section -> _dwarf_load_section -> _dwarf_load_debug_types -> _dwarf_load_die_containing_section -> _dwarf_next_cu_header_internal -> dwarf_next_cu_header_d -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` matches steps 1-4 by showing the freed pointer originated in the loaded `.debug_types` section before the harness freed it.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Step 1 loads the section bytes, step 2 returns a direct alias inside that section, step 3 stores the same pointer in `name`, and step 4 passes that pointer to `free()`.

poc.trigger: Run the staged `poc` through `fuzz_die_cu_attrs`; libdwarf loads `.debug_types`, `dwarf_diename()` returns a section-backed name pointer, and the vulnerable test source reaches `free(name)`.

format.name: ELF object with DWARF debug-types data
format.contract: The trigger is limited to the exact staged 279-byte witness at `gt_results/arvo_57429/poc` (sha256 `7e45353413b620d70e937a7ea5f7054577ad149493a7456f8c5d7a714c511326`). Under the staged vulnerable build, the harness writes those bytes verbatim to `/tmp/libfuzzer.$pid` and reopens them through libdwarf. The file must be admitted far enough that `dwarf_next_cu_header_d(..., is_info = 0)` causes `_dwarf_load_debug_types()` to allocate and populate the 48-byte `.debug_types` buffer seen in the saved ASan allocation stack, and later `dwarf_diename(cu_die, &name, errp)` must make `name` alias byte 29 of that buffer before line 185 executes `free(name)`. This contract is intentionally limited to this exact witness and observed runtime and does not claim a broader class of DWARF inputs.
